column2: Nilpotent obstructions and the real case For the actual Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of the tripod, the first obstruction is the integral cup product \(\delta_2(A,B)=A\cup B\). The next obstruction is a pair of triple Massey expressions with cyclotomic and action corrections, evaluated using compatible defining systems belonging to one chosen class-two lift. These are \citet[\S12.3.1, Proposition 7, author p.~14; Theorem 19 and Remark 20(ii), author pp.~21--22]{CohWickelgren2012}. There are non-point, noncuspidal rational abelian pairs with class-two sections already over \(\mathbb Q\), for example \((3,4)\) \citep[Propositions 24--25, author pp.~26--27]{CohWickelgren2012}. For arbitrary depth, the Massey-product necessary conditions in \citet[\S3.11 and Corollary 3.12, arXiv author pp.~16--17]{LitWickelgrenN2012} are stated with the coefficient primes dividing \(n!\) omitted. They are not an unrestricted integral all-depth converse at 2 and 3. The lower-central obstruction framework also appears in the opened \citet[pp.~1--2]{LitEllenberg2007} lecture notes. Those notes are a 2007 source, not the unpublished 2000 manuscript cited by later authors. Over \(\mathbb R\), the full profinite section classes of a hyperbolic curve are its real connected components \citep[Corollary 3.13, pp.~142--143]{LitMochizuki2003}. For a based real curve whose normalization components have real points, the abelian classes lifting to class two already identify these components \citep[Theorem 1.1, author p.~2]{LitWickelgrenReal2014}.

column2: The hypotheses of the nongeometric pro-prime results \citet[Theorem A, author pp.~3--4; Lemma 3.2, author p.~14]{LitHoshi2010} constructs nongeometric geometrically pro-\(p\) sections, for odd regular \(p\), on suitable geometric \(p\)-power covers of the tripod and their proper genus-at-least-two compactifications, after a finite extension inside the extension unramified outside \(p\) that is pro-\(p\) over \(\mathbb Q(\mu_p)\). The hypotheses include rational points and good reduction away from \(p\). This theorem does not assert the claimed construction simultaneously at every coefficient prime over \(\mathbb Q\). \citet[Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.5(i), article pp.~9--11]{LitHoshiTsujimura2021} gives a more explicit lifting statement for the tripod itself: let \(p\) be odd regular, let \(F\) be a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q\) or \(\mathbb Q_p\) containing \(\mu_p\), and let \(x_1,x_2\) be \(p\)-units in \(F\cap\Omega_{p\text{-unr}}\). Then their abelian pro-\(p\) Kummer section lifts to a full geometrically pro-\(p\) section. The infinity-cusp qualification in P.3 is needed before using that preprint's asserted nongeometricity criterion. \citet[condition $(*)$ and Theorem A, \S0, pp.~573--575]{LitSaidi2023} constructs nongeometric sections of certain geometrically pronilpotent-by-abelian quotients of proper curves over \(p\)-adic fields, after finite base extension. This is not a theorem about the full pronilpotent quotient over \(\mathbb Q\).

column2: The infinity cusp must be included in the 2021 criterion The implication from condition (3) to ``(2) or (4)'' in \citet[Proposition 1.4(ii), article p.~6]{LitHoshiTsujimura2021} omits the cusp at infinity and is false as printed. Consequently Theorem A(iii) and Corollary 2.5(iii) cannot be used without that qualification. The definition invoked there is \citet[Definition 1.1(iii), author p.~7]{LitHoshi2010}: geometricity means containment in a decomposition group of a rational point of the smooth compactification. The 2021 Theorem A(iii), article p.~3, repeats this definition explicitly; it includes the point at infinity. Here is the corrected tripod statement. For a number field or a finite extension \(F/\mathbb Q_p\), write \(D_p\subset F^\times\) for the kernel of the pro-\(p\) Kummer map; it consists of the roots of unity of order prime to \(p\). A pair of actual elements \((x_1,x_2)\in(F^\times)^2\) is the abelian image of at least one geometric geometrically pro-\(p\) section, where geometric includes cusps, if and only if at least one of the following holds: \[ \begin{array}{ll} \text{ordinary:}&\zeta_1x_1+\zeta_2x_2=1 \quad\text{for some }\zeta_1,\zeta_2\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }0:&x_2\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }1:&x_1\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }\infty:&-x_2/x_1\in D_p. \end{array} \] Thus the lift in P.2 is certainly nongeometric if all four conditions fail.

column2: Full pro-prime counterexamples over \(\mathbb Q\), including 2 Let \(p\) be 2 or an odd regular prime. There is a section of the full geometrically pro-\(p\) fundamental extension of the tripod over \(\mathbb Q\) with abelian pair \((\kappa_p(p),\kappa_p(p^2))\). Every such section is nongeometric, even allowing cusps. Its abelian pair is not ordinary at \(p\), so it is not a counterexample to either limit assertion for ordinary completed pairs. For odd regular \(p\), the same construction lifts every pair \((a\kappa_p(p),b\kappa_p(p))\), \(a,b\in\mathbb Z_p\). This is a derivation from the cited lifting and Galois-group theorems, not a claim that the quoted papers state this precise \(\mathbb Q\)-form.

column2: Unipotent Selmer results and the missing hypotheses Kim's theorem for the tripod proves finiteness of \(U(\mathbb Z[S^{-1}])\) for a fixed finite set \(S\), using rational unipotent fundamental groups and Selmer varieties \citep[\S3, concluding proof of Siegel's theorem, author pp.~17--18]{LitKim2005}. The conjecture of \citet[\S1.3 and Conjecture 3.1, author pp.~2--3 and 12; finite-$S$ variant in \S8]{LitBDCKW2018} asserts eventual equality of the associated local Chabauty--Kim locus with the integral points of the chosen model. These Selmer classes have fixed ramification and the stated local geometric and crystalline conditions. The strengthened comparison in \citet[Theorem A; Definition 2.1; \S2.2.1 and Lemma 2.19]{LitBKL2026} still concerns a fixed finite \(S\) and adelic, locally geometric sections. Its Theorem B and Corollary 5.17 establish the refined Chabauty--Kim conjecture for the tripod over \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\), for every odd coefficient prime. Its Remark 1.8 explicitly records that the corresponding full Selmer section assertion over \(\mathbb Q\), for the tripod and any finite \(S\), was already a consequence of \citet[Corollary 6, author p.~6]{Stix2015}. For the tripod there is a useful stronger local comparison: \citet[Lemma 4.2 and Corollary 4.3, author pp.~31--32]{LitBKL2026} shows that away from the coefficient prime \(p\), rational unipotent local cohomology is already determined by abelianization.

column2: Continuous cohomology and the scope of a derived-limit obstruction For \(T=\varprojlim_m T_m\), with finite discrete coefficient modules and surjective transition maps, continuous cohomology satisfies \[ 0\longrightarrow\varprojlim{}^1_m H^{i-1}(G,T_m) \longrightarrow H^i_{\rm cts}(G,T) \longrightarrow\varprojlim_m H^i(G,T_m)\longrightarrow0. \] This is \citet[equation (2.1) and Theorem (2.2), p.~215; Proposition (1.6), p.~211]{CohJannsen1988}. Finite cohomology groups at a local field, or with a fixed finite set of global ramification primes, make the relevant tower Mittag--Leffler and kill its \(\varprojlim^1\). Finiteness of the modules \(T_m\) alone does not imply finiteness of \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},T_m)\). In particular the unrestricted weight-two and weight-twelve computations in Part A require their separate arithmetic inputs and do not follow from Jannsen's formalism alone.

column2: Stronger full-section theorems do not remove the quotient gap For a hyperbolic curve over \(\mathbb Q\) with a nonconstant unit, \citet[Corollary 6, author p.~6]{Stix2015} identifies its full adelic section classes with rational points; Corollary 5, author p.~5, also handles noncuspidal Selmer sections having finite geometric support. For a smooth proper genus-at-least-two curve over a number field containing no CM subfield, \citet[Theorem A and Definition 1.1, author p.~1]{LitBettsStix2025} proves finiteness of the image at every finite place of the full Selmer section set. Neither statement is a theorem about arbitrary pronilpotent sections whose abelian localizations are ordinary.

column2: The precise local Hodge bridge for the tripod Let \(U_{p,n}\) be the depth-\(n\) rational \(\mathbb Q_p\)-unipotent geometric fundamental group of the tripod, based at \(0+1\), with its continuous \(G_{\mathbb Q_p}\)-action. Every class of \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_p},U_{p,n}(\mathbb Q_p))\) is semistable and hence de Rham. Moreover it is crystalline if and only if its abelian image is crystalline. Consequently, if a pro-\(p\) section has ordinary abelian image represented by \(x_p\), its rational unipotent image is semistable at every depth, and is crystalline when \(x_p,1-x_p\in\mathbb Z_p^\times\). These conclusions do not assert equality with the entire path torsor of \(x_p\).

column2: Brauer--Manin and descent comparisons \citet[Theorem 1.2, corrected author pp.~2--3; Remark 2.4, p.~7]{LitHarariSzamuely2009} characterizes the splitting of the Albanese quotient of the geometric abelian fundamental extension by membership of the Albanese torsor in the maximal divisible subgroup of \(H^1(k,\operatorname{Alb}_X)\). For curves the geometric abelianization itself is the relevant Tate module. The quasi-projective version uses the generalized Albanese. For a torsor under a semiabelian variety, finite Tate--Shafarevich group of its abelian quotient makes the indicated Brauer--Manin obstruction complete for existence of a rational point \citep[Theorem 1.1, author p.~2; Corollary 4.8 and Lemma 4.9, author p.~16]{LitHarariSzamuely2008}. For a geometrically connected variety over a number field and a continuous quotient of its geometric fundamental group whose kernel is normal in the arithmetic fundamental group, \citet[Theorem 2.1 and Remark (3), author pp.~11--12]{LitHarariStix2012} equates interpolation of a tuple of local point sections in that quotient with survival of the corresponding finite descent obstructions. This includes the full pronilpotent quotient and does not require an adelic tuple when formulated as that interpolation statement. Their Corollary 3.1, author p.~13, gives Brauer--Manin orthogonality on a proper curve from a section of its full geometric abelianization whose local sections come from points.

column2: Completed reciprocity complexes and their point domain \citet[Definitions 3.1--3.3, p.~728; Definition 3.10, p.~733]{LitPridham2020} defines adelic cohomology for profinite coefficients by a derived inverse limit of finite-coefficient restricted products, and compactly supported cohomology by the cocone of global restriction. The nilpotent reciprocity tower in Example 3.16, pp.~734--735, nevertheless starts from actual adelic points and requires a global quotient section matching their local path classes. column2: Density-zero reduction is weaker than finite prime support For a noncuspidal Selmer section of the \emph{full} arithmetic fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve over a number field, the primes where its local point reduces to a cusp have density zero after a suitable finite field extension. Two such sections with the same reductions on a set of density one are conjugate. These are \citet[Theorems~1.1--1.2, pp.1--2; Theorem~5.4 and Corollary~5.7, pp.14--15]{RootPorowski2025}. They supply neither a finite-support conclusion nor a theorem for an arbitrary geometrically pronilpotent section.

column2: The available Massey vanishing theorems do not supply the required compatible section Let $k$ be a number field and $p$ a prime. Every defined $n$-fold Massey product of classes in $H^1(k,\mathbb F_p(1))$, for $n\ge3$, contains zero, with the successive products interpreted in their appropriate Tate twists. This is the rank-one coefficient case of \citet[Theorem 7.4, author p.27]{RootHarpazWittenberg2023}. For trivial coefficients and odd $p$, if $\zeta_p\notin k$, the stronger condition that adjacent cups vanish suffices; it also suffices over the maximal tame Galois quotient \citep[Theorem 1.1]{RootMaireMinacRamakrishnaTan2026}. These are finite-coefficient conclusions with an existential choice of defining system. They do not assert liftability of every specified preceding section, simultaneous compatibility of all the obstruction coordinates for the actual tripod action, or compatible integral sections with one fixed ordinary pair. In particular they do not decide A.2, A.3, or the remainder in B.1.

column2: Comparison of the three survival assertions For an ordinary completed pair \(a=(A,B)\), write \(S_\ell(a)\) for existence of a section of the geometrically pro-\(\ell\) quotient \(E_U^{(\ell)}\) whose abelian class is \(a_\ell\). Write \(S_{r,\ell}(a)\) for its class-\(r\) version, \(S_r(a)\) for existence in \(E_U/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\), and \(S_{\rm nil}(a)\) for existence in \(E_U^{\rm nil}\). Then \[ S_{\rm nil}(a)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(\forall\ell\;S_\ell(a)\bigr) \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(\forall r\;S_r(a)\bigr). \] The pair is the same in every quantifier. Define \[ \begin{split} (\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}:\quad& \forall a\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord},\quad S_{\rm nil}(a)\Longrightarrow |\operatorname{supp}(a)|<\infty,\\ (\mathrm{FS})_\ell:\quad& \forall a\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord},\quad S_\ell(a)\Longrightarrow |\operatorname{supp}(a)|<\infty. \end{split} \] For any one prime \(\ell\), \((\mathrm{FS})_\ell\) implies \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\). A counterexample to the latter would be a counterexample to every \((\mathrm{FS})_\ell\), with the same pair. Counterexamples chosen separately for the different primes do not furnish that simultaneous counterexample.

column2: The main question and its single-prime versions We have neither proved \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\) nor constructed an ordinary infinite-support pair with a section of \(E_U^{\rm nil}\). We have also not decided \((\mathrm{FS})_2\), \((\mathrm{FS})_3\), or the assertion for arbitrary \(\ell\ge5\). These are the exact remaining assertions in tasks A2 and A3 and Lead L1. The fixed-pair equivalence in A.1 is a reduction to an integral class obstruction for each ghost; it is not an obstruction itself. At coefficient three, E.146--E.148 give an exact finite extension criterion: the old-support plus-character Frobenius equations, with every aligning frame retained. E.151 preserves an ordinary pair in the full power completion along any actually chosen infinite path through these systems. The missing assertion is existence or impossibility of such a compatible path. E.149 shows that individual frozen predecessors can fail, so an induction asserting that every node extends is false. This conditional construction concerns one specified support pattern; failure of that entire pattern would not by itself prove the general finite-support assertion. At coefficient two, E.155--E.159 remove the real obstruction for an actually boundary-matched ordinary predecessor and give an exact finite-parameter test for preserving every off-diagonal support match in the stated support pattern. Its passing infinite branch is not constructed. For every odd prime $\ell$ with $\ell\nmid h_{\mathbb Q(\zeta_\ell)}$, E.209 removes the fixed-ramification second-cohomology obstruction at every weight, including all weights at five. E.210 computes the exact integral first-cohomology correction groups and their localizations. E.212 proves that a failure of simultaneous matching in one fixed nonempty lifting fibre is witnessed by at most two support places. It supplies no bound on those places and no automatic compatibility. Thus, above a predecessor already matching all support points away from the coefficient prime, the next global lift exists and only the simultaneous matching condition remains. No infinite compatible sequence satisfying that condition has been constructed or excluded. This all-weight reduction does not settle any $(\mathrm{FS})_\ell$. E.171--E.174 do construct one ordinary infinite-support pair with a single integral class-two section matching every support point away from its coefficient prime, simultaneously for all coefficient primes; that section has an unrestricted global class-three lift. These assertions establish nonemptiness of the necessary class-two matching locus. They neither preserve point matching at class three nor supply any all-depth section, and they concern a different family from the original A.44 recursion. For the unchanged original recursion, E.213 and E.211 now construct a coefficient-five class-two section matching every support point, with a global class-three lift. The refinement in E.213 makes every individual next local matching constraint solvable; their two-vector residues still have to agree across all support primes. No such simultaneous agreement or higher matched lift has been established. Recovery update: E.214 proves selected original outputs first fail at pro-five class four. In a separate primitive-five family, E.215 constructs selected outputs with off-five point matching through class seven and a global class-eight lift. Neither closes this Open assertion.

column2: Why finite-ramification pro-prime constructions cannot be ghosts For an ordinary pair, its valuations are actual integers. If its \(\ell\)-primary abelian cocycle is unramified outside a finite set, then the pair has finite prime support and is a rational unit-equation pair. In particular, equality of its \(\ell\)-primary pair with that of a rational point, even at one coefficient prime, implies finite support. For a ghost, the ordinary valuation vectors outside every finite set span a rank-two subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^2\), and generate an open \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell^2\). Its pro-\(\ell\) abelian pair is not cuspidal. This confirms these assertions of GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.2.

column2: The exact conditional implication of a positive or negative limit answer If \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\) holds, every section of \(E_U\to G\) whose local sections at finite primes are ordinary is a rational-point section. Thus a positive answer would prove the locally ordinary case of Conjecture A, not merely reduce it to an unresolved rational-abelian-pair case. column2: The obstruction at an arbitrary integral class is a class of a specified lift Fix \(\ell\), a literal class-\(r\) cocycle \(c\), and the actual arithmetic action. A continuous Hall-coordinate section of \(N_{r+1,\ell}\twoheadrightarrow N_{r,\ell}\) gives a lift \(\widetilde c\) as a map of spaces. The formula \[ o_c(g,h)=\widetilde c(g)\,g\widetilde c(h)\, \widetilde c(gh)^{-1} \] defines a continuous two-cocycle in \(L_{r+1,\ell}=\mathbb Z_\ell(r+1)^{b_{r+1}}\). Its class vanishes precisely when \(c\) lifts. It depends on the class-\(r\) section as well as on the abelian pair. Its projections to finite coefficients need not determine whether this continuous class vanishes.

column2: Compatibility, prescribed symmetries, and the ambiguity of a lift Let \(X\) be a compact space of candidates, and let \(X_i\subseteq X\) be closed subsets expressing specified finite conditions. If every finite collection of these conditions has a simultaneous solution in \(X\), they have a common solution. Consequently any purported example in which all finite cofinal tests of one fixed closed lifting-and-symmetry problem succeed, but the problem has no solution, must fail one of these hypotheses. For sections, a chosen lift through a central kernel \(T\), if it exists, leaves the torsor under \(H^1(G,T)\) undetermined. This is the relevant test of the comparisons proposed in R9.

column2: All-depth survival alone does not bound ramification Choose distinct rational primes \(q_j\), and put \(A=\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!}\) in the power completion. There is an actual full profinite cuspidal section of the tripod with abelian pair \((A,1)\). It has infinite support and ramifies at infinitely many primes in every coefficient component. Its pair is not ordinary. Thus finite ramification cannot follow from all-depth lifting alone; any proof of A2 must use the ordinary local unit equation.

column2: Compactness with the abelian cocycle fixed For $r\geq2$, $Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,\mathbb Z_\ell(r))$ is a finite free $\mathbb Z_\ell$-module, compact for the compact-open topology. Fix a literal cocycle $a\in Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,N_{1,\ell})$. Then the space \[ \mathscr S_{r,\ell}(a)= \{c\in Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,N_{r,\ell}):c_{\rm ab}=a\} \] is compact Hausdorff. More precisely, it is parametrized continuously by a closed subset of a finite power of $\mathbb Z_\ell$, with Hall coordinates polynomial over $\mathbb Q_\ell$ in the parameters and continuous cochains as coefficients. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.3--C.1.6. No compactness is asserted when $a$ varies.

column2: The exact limit equivalence and its quantifiers Fix $(A,B)\in(\widehat{\mathbb Q^{\times}})^2$. For the tripod over $\mathbb Q$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of $E_U^{\rm nil}\to G_{\mathbb Q}$; \item for every prime $\ell$, its $\ell$-component is the abelianization of a continuous section of the full geometrically pro-$\ell$ quotient; \item for every positive integer $r$, the same pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of the integral class-$r$ quotient; \item for every $\ell$ and every $r$, the same $\ell$-component survives the pro-$\ell$ class-$r$ quotient. \end{enumerate} The corresponding fixed-$\ell$ equivalence holds. It continues to hold after imposing geometric conjugacy to one prescribed compatible family of local point sections, or local cuspidal sections, at every level. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.7. The assertion does not permit the pair to change with $r$ or $\ell$.

column2: A projective quotient retaining the cyclotomic character kills off-diagonal tame inertia Let \(K\) be a number field, \(\ell\) a prime, and \(\psi:G_K\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma\) a continuous quotient. Assume that \(\Gamma\) has an open pro-\(\ell\) subgroup, that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell\Gamma\leq1\), and that the \(\ell\)-adic cyclotomic character factors continuously through \(\psi\). Then, at each finite place \(v\nmid\ell\), the \(\ell\)-primary tame inertia has trivial image in \(\Gamma\) after passage to any finite extension making the local image pro-\(\ell\). In particular, suppose that the actual tangential action on \(F_\ell\), and a continuous section cocycle \(G_{\mathbb Q}\to F_\ell\), factor through such a quotient of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\). column2: Every ordinary completed pair has support of upper relative prime density zero Let \((A,B)\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) be an ordinary completed pair over \(\mathbb Q\). No nonabelian section is assumed. If \(S\) is its support, then \[ \limsup_{X\longrightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{p\in S:p\le X\}}{\pi(X)}=0, \tag{A.33.1} \] where \(\pi(X)\) counts all rational primes up to \(X\). Thus the density is relative to the primes, not the ordinary integer density shared by every set of primes. More precisely, partition the support into the three disjoint sets \[ \begin{split} S_0&=\{p:v_p(A)>0\},\qquad S_1=\{p:v_p(B)>0\},\\ S_\infty&=\{p:v_p(A)=v_p(B)<0\}, \end{split} \tag{A.33.2} \] and put \(C_0=B\), \(C_1=A\), \(C_\infty=-A/B\). If \(v_{p_i}(C_i)=m_i\ne0\), then for every squarefree positive integer \(N\) coprime to \(p_i m_i\), \[ \limsup_{X\longrightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{p\in S_i:p\le X\}}{\pi(X)} \le \frac{\varphi(N)}{N}. \tag{A.33.3} \] If any of these three \(C_i\) has no nonzero valuation, the pair is one of the rational pairs treated explicitly in the proof. In particular the density conclusion cannot distinguish an ordinary ghost from a full-tower survivor: it holds before any survival test.

column2: Geometry of every odd-prime Heisenberg cover Let \(\ell\) be odd and \(t_0\in U(\mathbb Q)\). Let \(H_\ell\) be the universal two-generator quotient of class at most two and exponent dividing \(\ell\). It is the group of upper unitriangular \(3\times3\) matrices over \(\mathbb F_\ell\), of order \(\ell^3\). The inverse image of the point section at \(t_0\) in the arithmetic \(H_\ell\)-quotient defines a connected finite etale cover \(Y_{\ell,t_0}\to U\) of degree \(\ell^3\), with a specified rational point above \(t_0\). Its compactification has \[ g(\overline Y_{\ell,t_0})=1+\frac{\ell^2(\ell-3)}2, \qquad |\overline Y_{\ell,t_0}\setminus Y_{\ell,t_0}|=3\ell^2. \] Its central quotient is the pointed diagonal curve \[ C_{\ell,t_0}:\quad t_0 u^\ell+(1-t_0)v^\ell=1, \qquad (u,v)=(1,1), \] and \(\overline Y_{\ell,t_0}\to\overline C_{\ell,t_0}\) is an unramified cover of degree \(\ell\). Thus the genus-one case \(\ell=3\) is exceptional; the genera at \(\ell=5,7\) are already \(26,99\).

column2: The exponent-prime degree formula cannot include two unchanged There is no nonabelian group of exponent two. In particular the universal rank-two class-two exponent-two quotient has order four, not eight. If ``Heisenberg at two'' instead means \(\mathrm U_3(\mathbb F_2)\), that group has exponent four and is dihedral of order eight. A cover with branch generators its two standard involutions has branch orders \((2,2,4)\), genus zero, and ten boundary points. These are two different conventions, and neither is obtained by substituting two into the odd-prime exponent-\(\ell\) assertion. The exponent-two quotient instead has genus zero and six boundary points. A pointed degree-eight dihedral model above \(t_0=3\) is explicit: \[ \begin{gathered} a(s)=\frac{1+6s^2}{1-6s^2},\qquad b(s)=\frac{2s}{1-6s^2},\\ u(s)=a(s)^2+6b(s)^2+4a(s)b(s),\qquad v(s)=a(s)^2+6b(s)^2+6a(s)b(s),\\ t(s)=3u(s)^2,\qquad 1-t(s)=-2v(s)^2. \end{gathered} \] The point \(s=0\) lies over \(t=3\). The open source is \(\mathbb P^1_s\) with the ten points above \(0,1,\infty\) removed.

column2: Passing to a cover preserves the appropriate prime, not every prime Let \(Y\to U\) be a connected geometrically Galois cover whose geometric group is a nontrivial \(p\)-group of order \(d\). If a geometrically pro-\(p\) section factors through its associated open arithmetic subgroup, that subgroup is the full geometrically pro-\(p\) arithmetic fundamental group of \(Y\). For the full pronilpotent group of \(U\), the induced geometric open subgroup is instead \[ K_p\times\prod_{\ell\ne p}F_\ell, \qquad [F_p:K_p]=d. \] It is not the full pronilpotent geometric fundamental group of \(Y\). For \(\ell\ne p\), the latter has free pro-\(\ell\) rank \(d+1\), whereas the inherited factor has rank two.

column2: The missing pointwise hypothesis in an all-prime pointed-cover test Fix \(t_0\in U(\mathbb Q)\). Suppose an ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\) has, for every prime \(\ell\), the same reduction modulo \(\ell\)-th powers as \((t_0,1-t_0)\). Then \((A,B)=(\kappa(t_0),\kappa(1-t_0))\). In particular, factorization of a single section through the point-\(t_0\) Heisenberg cover at every prime would already force its ordinary abelian pair to be rational. Such factorization is not an automatic property of a full section: the rational-point section at two does not factor through the point-three Heisenberg cover at five.

column2: Exact local images for the variable exponent Let $d\ge2$, let $24\mid C$, and choose $h\ge2d^2$ at least every prime divisor of $C$. Set \[ n=h!,\qquad E(Z)=Cn\prod_{r=2}^d(Z^r-1),\qquad D=Cd!n^d. \] For $p\mid n$, put $v=v_p(n)$, $e=v_p(d)$, and $a_p=1$ for odd $p$, $a_2=2$. Then the map \[ F_p(z)=\exp(E(z)\log z) \] is a bijection \[ 1+p^v+p^{v+a_p}\mathbb Z_p \xrightarrow{\sim} F_p(1+p^v)(1+p^{W_p}\mathbb Z_p),\qquad W_p=v_p(C)+(d+1)v+v_p(d!)+a_p+e. \tag{E.30.1} \] It preserves congruences, agrees with $z^{E(z)}$ on positive integer inputs, and throughout this shell \[ v_p(z-1)=v,\qquad v_p(E(z))=v_p(D),\qquad W_p\le2v_p(D). \tag{E.30.2} \] For $p\nmid n$, let $\omega\in\mu_{p-1}(\mathbb Z_p)$ satisfy $\omega^r\not\equiv1\pmod p$ for $2\le r\le d$. For a fixed integer $e_0$ modulo $p-1$, the map \[ z\longmapsto \omega^{e_0} \exp(E(z)\log(z/\omega)) \tag{E.30.3} \] is a congruence-preserving bijection from $\omega(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$ to $\omega^{e_0}(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$. It equals the ordinary variable power on those positive integer inputs for which $E(z)\equiv e_0$ modulo $p-1$.

column2: Uniform Hall, inertia, and arithmetic-kernel bounds Fix $R\ge3$. Let $N_r=\Pi/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi$ and $L_r=\Gamma_r\Pi/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi=\widehat{\mathbb Z}(r)^{b_r}$. Use the actual point-three section $s_3$ to identify $E_r=N_r\rtimes_{\rho_3}G_{\mathbb Q}$. Define \[ K_r(m)=\ker\left(N_r\longrightarrow (1+I)((\mathbb Z/m)\langle X,Y\rangle/I^{r+1})\right), \qquad I=(X,Y), \tag{E.32.1} \] using the integral Magnus images $x\mapsto1+X$, $y\mapsto1+Y$. If $h_R$ is the number of Hall basis elements through weight $R$, put \[ D_H=(R!)^{h_R+1},\quad T=2(R!)^R,\quad B_r=2|K_{2r-2}(\mathbb Z)|\quad(2\le r\le R). \tag{E.32.2} \] Then $K_r(m)$ is characteristic, the continuous Hall set section $\sigma_r:N_{r-1}\to N_r$ with zero new coordinates satisfies \[ \sigma_r(K_{r-1}(D_Hm))\subset K_r(m), \tag{E.32.3} \] and the finite integer $B_r$ annihilates $H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_\ell(r))$ for every coefficient prime $\ell$. At a fresh prime $q>3$, $q\ne\ell$, suppose an ordinary local abelian pair has valuation pattern $(E,0)$, $(0,E)$, or $(-E,-E)$. For any actual class-$(r-1)$ section with this pair, the central defect $c$ of its canonical Hall set lift satisfies the strict tame-residue bound \[ \frac{z_q(c)}{q^{r-1}-1} \in \frac{E}{T\prod_{k=2}^{r-1}(q^k-1)} \mathbb Z_\ell^{b_r}. \tag{E.32.4} \] The product is empty for $r=2$. column2: The relative Bloch component, its harmonic cancellation, and a nonzero ghost example Let $q\ge5$ be a support prime of an ordinary pair, and let $\ell$ be an odd prime dividing $q+1$. For $\ell\ge5$ there is no global twist ambiguity. For $\ell=3$, the ambiguity is exactly the order-three subgroup generated by the localization of $\eta$. The resulting quotient class is therefore an invariant of the ordinary completed pair. This is a relative class defined by its global central primitive and the local point comparison; it has not been identified with the single symbol of the point's reduction at a cusp. There are infinite-support ordinary pairs for which this relative Bloch quotient is nonzero. More precisely, a modification of the E.123 recursion has a $B$-support prime $r$ with $v_3(r^2-1)=2$ at which $D_{r,3}$ has order nine for every global integral class-two section. Thus none of the twenty-four global classes matches there, although the prescribed ordinary point reduces to the cusp one. There is also an exact harmonic cancellation for the rational reference point $t=1/2$: for every $\ell\ge5$ and every $q\ne2,\ell$ with $\ell\nmid q-1$, its integral class-two local section equals the unit tangential section at zero. Write \(Z_i(g)\in\mathbb F_3^3\) for the central component of \(j_{0,i}(g)\bmod3\), put \[ k_q=\frac{q^4-1}{3}\bmod3\in\mathbb F_3^\times , \qquad Z(g)=\bigl(Z_1(g)\ Z_2(g)\bigr), \tag{E.131.1} \] and use the \(H_9\)-aligned Frobenius representative already prescribed in E.125. The actual action on \(W_n\) factors through \(\chi_3\bmod3\), and hence \[ W_n/B_n=C_n^+\oplus C_n^-, \qquad C_n^+\simeq\mathbb F_3^{\,a_n},\quad C_n^-\simeq\mathbb F_3(1)^{\,d_n}. \tag{E.144.2} \] Retain the actual action on \(Q_n\) in a finite arithmetic quotient \(D\), unramified outside three. Suppose it matches specified ordinary point sections at every old place in \(S\). Any extension of \(\rho\) to \(Q_n\rtimes D\) which retains these old local point conditions, and whose local class at each newly ramified prime is the image of an ordinary point section, must induce a solution \[ \bar\rho:G_{\mathbb Q,S}\longrightarrow (Q_n/B_n)\rtimes D \tag{E.144.3} \] which retains all these old local point conditions. column2: The pro-two comparison and the one-prime free product Let \(S=\{2,\infty,q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\), where the \(q_i\) are distinct odd primes. Write \(G_S\) for the full Galois group unramified outside \(S\), and \(G_S(2)\) for its maximal pro-two quotient. Inflation and local restriction give isomorphisms \[ H^2(G_S(2),\mathbb F_2) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^2(G_S,\mathbb F_2) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^2(\mathbb R,\mathbb F_2) \oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^t H^2(\mathbb Q_{q_i},\mathbb F_2). \tag{E.185.1} \] Each summand on the right has order two. There is a minimal pro-two presentation with generators \(c,a,x_1,\ldots,x_t\) and defining relations \[ c^2=1,\qquad y_i x_i y_i^{-1}=x_i^{q_i}\quad(1\leq i\leq t). \tag{E.185.2} \] Here \(c\) maps to complex conjugation, \(x_i\) to a chosen generator of tame inertia at \(q_i\), and \(y_i\) is a word mapping to an actual arithmetic Frobenius at that same prime. The generator \(a\) can be chosen dual modulo the Frattini subgroup to \(\kappa_2(2)\), with its other Kummer coordinates zero. The words \(y_i\) are not independent generators. For \(t=0\), the group is \(C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}\mathbb Z_2\). For \(t=1\) and \(q_1\equiv3\) or \(5\pmod8\), one may replace \(a\) by the actual Frobenius at \(q_1\), obtaining \[ G_{\{2,q_1,\infty\}}(2) \simeq C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2} \bigl(\mathbb Z_2\rtimes_{q_1}\mathbb Z_2\bigr) = C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}G_{\mathbb Q_{q_1}}(2). \tag{E.185.3} \] The two indicated factors are the actual real and chosen local decomposition groups.
